cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintPages
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind the PrintPages collection: the pages queued in the application-wide multi-document print job (Application.PrintJob.Pages). It only reports how many pages are queued (Count) and returns one queued page by index (Item); pages are added through the print job, not here.
use_for: checking how many pages a batch print job will output before sending it
walking the queued pages of a multi-document proof run
avoid: printing a single document: use Document.PrintSettings and PrintSettings.PrintOut; this collection belongs to the multi-document PrintJob
adding or removing pages here: no such members; use the print job's AddPage / AddDocument / Clear
cards.how: Reached as Application.PrintJob.Pages (the Pages property of the print job); the visible VBA class name is PrintPages. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of pages currently queued in the print job

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: one queued page (IPrnVBAPrintPage) by index; hidden but the default member (dispid 0), so Pages(i) and Pages.Item(i) are the same call

gotchas: no _NewEnum member is harvested, so For Each over the collection is not available; loop For i = 1 To Count
index base is 1 like the other CorelDRAW collections (unverified)
this is the application-wide PrintJob, not a document's PrintSettings; queued pages stay until the job's Clear is called (unverified)
cards.example:
Set job = Application.PrintJob
Debug.Print job.Pages.Count & " pages queued"
For i = 1 To job.Pages.Count
    Set pg = job.Pages.Item(i)
Next i

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintPostScript
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind PrintSettings.PostScript: the PostScript tab of CorelDRAW's Print dialog. It sets the PostScript level, DSC conformance, JPEG compression of bitmaps, font download (Type 1, TrueType to Type 1), OPI / DCS link handling, curve complexity (max nodes per curve, flatness), fountain-fill step tuning, screen frequency, and the PDF options used if the PostScript is distilled later.
use_for: preparing a .prn / .ps file for an imagesetter or RIP
PostScript Level 3 output for a print shop that distills to PDF
getting past RIP limitcheck errors on very complex curves (MaxPointsPerCurve, AutoIncreaseFlatness)
smoother gradients in print (AutoIncreaseFountainSteps)
keeping OPI links for a prepress workflow that swaps in high-res images
avoid: making a PDF directly: use Document.PublishToPDF with Document.PDFSettings; the PDF* switches here only matter when the PostScript is distilled afterwards
JPEGCompression on high-end proofs or fine line art in bitmaps: lossy; leave it off
non-PostScript printers: these settings only apply to PostScript output
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings.PostScript (or Application.PrintJob.Settings.PostScript): a read-only reference to the settings object whose properties you set. Visible VBA class name: PrintPostScript. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: ConformToDSC
key_members.use: generate DSC-compliant PostScript only (needed by many imposition / RIP tools)

key_members.name: JPEGCompression
key_members.use: JPEG-compress bitmaps in the stream (smaller, lossy)

key_members.name: JPEGQuality
key_members.use: JPEG quality factor used when JPEGCompression is on

key_members.name: DownloadType1
key_members.use: download Type 1 fonts to the device

key_members.name: TrueTypeToType1
key_members.use: convert TrueType fonts to Type 1 before downloading

key_members.name: MaintainOPILinks
key_members.use: keep OPI links so the RIP / OPI server substitutes high-res images

key_members.name: ResolveDCSLinks
key_members.use: resolve DCS links into the output

key_members.name: MaxPointsPerCurve
key_members.use: maximum nodes per curve; complex curves are split above it

key_members.name: Flatness
key_members.use: curve flatness (higher = fewer segments, coarser curves)

key_members.name: AutoIncreaseFlatness
key_members.use: raise flatness automatically when a curve is too complex for the device

key_members.name: AutoIncreaseFountainSteps
key_members.use: add fountain steps for long colour transitions (less banding)

key_members.name: OptimizeFountainFills
key_members.use: drop fountain steps for short transitions (faster output)

key_members.name: PDFStartup
key_members.use: PrnPDFStartup: how a PDF distilled from this PostScript opens

key_members.name: PDFHyperlinks
key_members.use: include hyperlinks for a PDF distilled from this PostScript

key_members.name: pdfBookmarks
key_members.use: include bookmarks for a PDF distilled from this PostScript

gotchas: the typelib spells pdfBookmarks in lower camel case while its siblings are PascalCase; VBA ignores case, case-sensitive early-bound wrappers (Python makepy) do not (unverified)
JPEGQuality has no harvested range; check in the Print dialog which end means best quality before scripting it (unverified)
with a non-PostScript (GDI) printer selected and no PPD, these settings are ignored (unverified)
a high Flatness visibly facets large curves on big output (unverified)
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.PostScript
    .Level = prnPSLevel3
    .ConformToDSC = True
    .JPEGCompression = False
    .DownloadType1 = True
    .AutoIncreaseFountainSteps = True
End With

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintPrepress
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind PrintSettings.Prepress: the Prepress tab of the Print dialog. It controls film output (Invert for a negative, Mirror for emulsion side), printer's marks (crop / fold marks, exterior-only crop marks, registration marks and their style, colour calibration bar, densitometer scale and its density steps) and the slug line (file info, job name, page numbers, inside or outside the page), optionally placed around the objects instead of the page.
use_for: print-ready proofs with crop and registration marks
film or plate output that needs a negative or mirrored (emulsion-down) image
press checks with a colour bar and a densitometer scale
a slug line with job name and page numbers on every sheet
avoid: marks on paper the same size as the page: they fall outside the printable area; print on larger paper
Invert / Mirror for an ordinary paper proof: you get a negative, mirrored print
adding bleed: not here; set PrintSettings.Layout.UseBleedLimit and BleedLimit
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings.Prepress: a read-only reference to the settings object; set its properties. Visible VBA class name: PrintPrepress. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: RegistrationStyle
key_members.use: PrnRegistrationStyle: prnStandard, prnLong, prnSquare, prnHalfInverted, prnCorel

key_members.name: Densities
key_members.use: indexed: density value of each densitometer step

key_members.name: InfoWithinPage
key_members.use: put file info and page numbers inside the page area

key_members.name: MarksToObjects
key_members.use: place prepress marks around the objects instead of the page

gotchas: Densities is an indexed property (Densities(i)); the number of steps and the index base are not in the harvest (unverified)
JobName only appears on the sheet when FileInfo is on (unverified)
MarksToObjects moves crop marks to the objects' bounds, which is wrong for a page with intentional empty margins (unverified)
marks that do not fit the paper are clipped without an error (unverified)
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Prepress
    .CropMarks = True
    .RegistrationMarks = True
    .RegistrationStyle = prnStandard
    .ColorCalibrationBar = True
    .FileInfo = True
    .JobName = "Poster A2 v3"
End With

review.changes: avoid: bleed now points at the real members PrintSettings.Layout.UseBleedLimit / BleedLimit instead of vague "layout settings"

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintSeparations
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind PrintSettings.Separations: the separation settings of the Print dialog. It turns colour separation on (one plate per ink), prints plates in colour, chooses hexachrome, converts spot colours to process, prints or skips empty plates, preserves document overprints and always overprints black, runs CorelDRAW's own auto-spread trapping (amount, fixed width, minimum text size), sets the advanced screening (imaging resolution, basic screen, halftone dot, screening technology) and returns the plate list.
use_for: film or plate separations for offset or screen printing
converting spot colours to CMYK for a process-only job (SpotToCMYK)
black text overprinting to hide misregistration halos (AlwaysOverprintBlack)
checking or switching off individual ink plates through Plates
avoid: separations for a modern PDF workflow: send a composite PDF and let the RIP separate
Hexachrome on current presses: a legacy six-colour system; use CMYK
in-RIP trapping: that lives in PrintSettings.Trapping; AutoSpreading here is CorelDRAW's own trapping
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings.Separations: a read-only reference to the settings object. Visible VBA class name: PrintSeparations. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: InColor
key_members.use: print each plate in its ink colour instead of black

key_members.name: SpotToCMYK
key_members.use: convert spot colours to process plates

key_members.name: PreserveOverprints
key_members.use: keep the overprints set in the document

key_members.name: AutoSpreadTextAbove
key_members.use: smallest text point size that is still trapped

gotchas: BasicScreen, HalftoneType and ScreenTechnology are free strings: the value must match an entry the dialog offers for the selected printer / PPD (unverified)
Resolution and the screening strings are only used with AdvancedSettings = True (unverified)
the Plates list follows the inks used in the document and the SpotToCMYK / Hexachrome switches; re-read Plates after changing them (unverified)
AutoSpreading plus in-RIP trapping (PrintSettings.Trapping) can trap twice (unverified)
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Separations
    .Enabled = True
    .SpotToCMYK = False
    .EmptyPlates = False
    .PreserveOverprints = True
    .AlwaysOverprintBlack = True
End With

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintSettings
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind a document's PrintSettings object: the whole Print dialog as an object. It picks the printer (or a PPD), print-to-file with file name and file mode (single file, one per page, one per plate), what to print (whole document, current page, selection, page range), copies and collation, paper size and orientation, and holds the Separations, Prepress, PostScript, Trapping, Options and Layout sub-settings; it loads and saves print styles, resets, shows the dialog, and prints without the dialog.
use_for: unattended printing of proofs or production sheets from a script
writing PostScript / PRN files to disk for a RIP (PrintToFile)
applying one saved print style to many documents (Load)
one output file per plate for film (FileMode = prnSeparatePlates)
avoid: Document.PrintOut in unattended runs: the typelib says it opens the Print dialog; call PrintSettings.PrintOut
ShowDialog in a COM pipeline: modal, the call blocks until a person closes it
making PDFs: use Document.PublishToPDF, not a PDF printer driver
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings (one per document; set properties on it), or Application.PrintJob.Settings for a multi-document job. Visible VBA class name: PrintSettings. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: Reset
key_members.use: back to default settings; do this first for repeatable jobs

key_members.name: SelectPrinter
key_members.use: choose the destination printer by its installed name

key_members.name: Printer
key_members.use: the destination printer object (putref; one of Application.Printers)

key_members.name: UsePPD
key_members.use: use a PPD file instead of the driver's description

key_members.name: PrintToFile
key_members.use: write the job to a file instead of the device

key_members.name: PageRange
key_members.use: page range string used with prnPageRange

key_members.name: SetCustomPaperSize
key_members.use: custom paper width, height and orientation

key_members.name: Load
key_members.use: load a saved print style; returns True on success

key_members.name: PrintOut
key_members.use: print with the current settings, no dialog

gotchas: PageRange is only used when PrintRange = prnPageRange (unverified)
Printer is a putref object property: in VBA write Set .Printer = ..., or just call SelectPrinter with the exact installed name
settings stay on the document between jobs; call Reset first so an earlier job's separations or marks do not leak in (unverified)
the PrintToFile format follows the selected driver: pick a PostScript printer or UsePPD for a real .prn / .ps file (unverified)
PaperWidth and PaperHeight are read-only; change the size with SetPaperSize or SetCustomPaperSize
Load and Save return a Boolean instead of raising; check the result (unverified)
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings
    .Reset
    .SelectPrinter "My PostScript Printer"  ' exact installed name
    .PrintToFile = True
    .FileName = "E:\out\poster.prn"
    .PrintRange = prnPageRange: .PageRange = "1-2"
    .PrintOut
End With

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintTrapping
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind PrintSettings.Trapping: in-RIP trapping settings written into the PostScript for a PostScript device whose RIP does the trapping. It turns in-RIP trapping on, sets trap width and black trap width, trap colour scaling, step limit, black colour and density limits, sliding trap limit, how traps meet bitmaps (ImageTrap), object-to-image, internal image and mono bitmap trapping, and holds the per-ink trap layers.
use_for: offset jobs where the print shop's RIP does in-RIP trapping and wants it requested in the file
hiding misregistration gaps between adjoining spot and process colours
per-ink neutral density and trap order through Layers
avoid: devices without in-RIP trapping: use Separations.AutoSpreading or let the print shop trap
when the print shop already traps in its own workflow: double trapping shows as dark outlines
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings.Trapping: a read-only reference to the settings object. Visible VBA class name: PrintTrapping. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: Width
key_members.use: how far one colour spreads into another

key_members.name: BlackWidth
key_members.use: how far black spreads into other colours

key_members.name: StepLimit
key_members.use: step limit threshold for creating a trap

key_members.name: BlackColorLimit
key_members.use: black ink density at which a colour counts as pure black for trapping

key_members.name: SlidingTrapLimit
key_members.use: density difference at which the trap slides toward the centreline

gotchas: units of Width / BlackWidth are not in the harvest; read the dialog's units before scripting values (unverified)
Layers.Item has dispid 2, not the default dispid 0, so write Layers.Item(i) rather than Layers(i)
in-RIP trapping only exists in the PostScript stream; it has no effect on non-PostScript output (unverified)
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Trapping
    .Enabled = True
    .ImageTrap = prnTrapSpread
    .ObjectsToImage = True
    .TrapMonoBitmaps = False
    Debug.Print .Width, .BlackWidth, .Layers.Count
End With

review.changes: summary: dropped the unharvested "PostScript 3" claim; BlackColorLimit use says density (batch wording) instead of percentage

cards.name: IPrnVBASeparationPlate
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind one SeparationPlate of PrintSettings.Separations.Plates: a single ink plate of a separated print job. It reports the plate's colour name and lets a script switch the plate on or off, set its halftone screen frequency and angle, and choose whether text and graphics overprint on that plate.
use_for: skipping a plate when only one ink needs new film
custom screen angles / frequencies per ink to avoid moire
overprinting text or graphics on a spot plate such as a varnish or white underprint
avoid: Type: the typelib calls it reserved for future use; identify plates by Color
plate edits while separations are off: set Separations.Enabled first (unverified)
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings.Separations.Plates(i) (Plates.Item(i)). Visible VBA class name: SeparationPlate. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: Color
key_members.use: read-only colour (ink) name of the plate

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: PrnPlateType, read-only; reserved for future use

gotchas: Type is documented as reserved; do not branch on it
per-plate Frequency / Angle may only be used with Separations.AdvancedSettings = True (unverified)
Color is the ink name as the dialog shows it (a Pantone name for spot plates); match it exactly (unverified)
cards.example:
Set seps = ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Separations
seps.Enabled = True
For i = 1 To seps.Plates.Count
    With seps.Plates.Item(i)
        Debug.Print .Color, .Frequency, .Angle, .Enabled
    End With
Next i

cards.name: IPrnVBASeparationPlates
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind the SeparationPlates collection (PrintSettings.Separations.Plates): the ink plates available for the document's separations. Count gives the number of plates and Item(i) returns one plate.
use_for: listing the inks a job will separate into before sending it to film
a pre-press check that a job carries only the expected spot plates
avoid: adding or removing inks: no such members; the plates come from the colours used in the document
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings.Separations.Plates (read-only). Visible VBA class name: SeparationPlates. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of separation plates for this document

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: one plate (SeparationPlate) by index; default member (dispid 0), so Plates(i) works

gotchas: no _NewEnum member is harvested, so For Each is not available; loop For i = 1 To Count
index base is 1 (unverified)
the list changes with Separations.SpotToCMYK / Hexachrome; re-read it after switching (unverified)
cards.example:
Set plates = ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Separations.Plates
For i = 1 To plates.Count
    Debug.Print i, plates.Item(i).Color
Next i

cards.name: IPrnVBATrapLayer
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind one TrapLayer of PrintSettings.Trapping.Layers: the in-RIP trapping settings of one ink, i.e. its colour name, neutral density, trap type (normal, transparent, opaque, opaque-ignore) and its place in the trapping order.
use_for: metallic or opaque spot inks that other colours should not trap into (prnLayerOpaque / prnLayerOpaqueIgnore)
transparent varnish inks (prnLayerTransparent)
setting the trap order and neutral density of spot inks
avoid: Type: reserved for future use; identify the ink by Color
edits while PrintSettings.Trapping.Enabled is off: nothing is trapped
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings.Trapping.Layers.Item(i). Visible VBA class name: TrapLayer. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: Color
key_members.use: read-only ink name of this trap layer

key_members.name: Density
key_members.use: neutral density of the ink (decides which colour spreads into which)

key_members.name: Order
key_members.use: position of this ink in the trapping order

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: PrnPlateType, read-only; reserved for future use

gotchas: a wrong Density flips which colour spreads into which; use the ink maker's neutral density values (unverified)
whether Order values must be unique is not in the harvest (unverified)
cards.example:
Set tr = ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Trapping
For i = 1 To tr.Layers.Count
    With tr.Layers.Item(i)
        Debug.Print .Color, .Density, .Order
        .TrapType = prnLayerNormal
    End With
Next i

cards.name: IPrnVBATrapLayers
cards.summary: Hidden interface behind the TrapLayers collection (PrintSettings.Trapping.Layers): one in-RIP trap layer per ink. Count gives the number of layers and Item(i) returns one.
use_for: walking all inks to set trap type and order before in-RIP trapped output
avoid: adding or removing layers: no such members; the layers follow the document's inks
cards.how: Document.PrintSettings.Trapping.Layers (read-only). Visible VBA class name: TrapLayers. The IPrnVBA interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb (also in the CdrPrn library); object browsers show the visible coclass name instead, and the members work as listed.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: one TrapLayer by index (dispid 2, not the default member)

gotchas: Item has dispid 2 instead of the default dispid 0, so Layers(i) may fail; write Layers.Item(i)
no _NewEnum member is harvested, so For Each is not available; loop For i = 1 To Count
index base is 1 (unverified)
cards.example:
Set trapLayers = ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Trapping.Layers
For i = 1 To trapLayers.Count
    Debug.Print i, trapLayers.Item(i).Color
Next i

cards.name: IStructImportCropOptions
cards.summary: Options object CorelDRAW hands to an import crop handler (IImportCropHandler.Crop) when a bitmap is imported in crop mode: read-only facts about the source file (FileName, FilterID, CustomData, ImageWidth, ImageHeight, DpiX, DpiY) and the writable crop rectangle (Left, Top, Width, Height) the handler fills in. The typelib gives no member descriptions, so the roles follow the names and read-only flags.
use_for: batch-importing photos cropped per file by a rule (square product shots, fixed aspect banners)
cropping scans on import based on each image's pixel size or DPI
avoid: the same crop for every file: set StructImportOptions.Mode = cdrImportCrop and its CropLeft / CropTop / CropWidth / CropHeight instead of writing a handler
when the full image must stay in the file: import whole and crop with a PowerClip
cards.how: Not created by scripts: an object implementing IImportCropHandler is set as StructImportOptions.CropHandler, Mode is cdrImportCrop, and CorelDRAW passes this object to its Crop method during Layer.ImportEx (flow unverified).

key_members.name: CustomData
key_members.use: read-only: caller data passed through to the handler

gotchas: every member is a long integer: crop values are most likely source pixels, not document units (unverified)
CustomData is presumably StructImportOptions.CustomData passed through so one handler can serve several imports (unverified)
Crop returns a Boolean; what returning False does (skip the crop or cancel the import) is not in the harvest (unverified)
implementing IImportCropHandler needs Implements in a VBA class module or a registered COM object from outside (unverified)
cards.example:
' VBA class module, set as StructImportOptions.CropHandler (unverified)
Implements IImportCropHandler
Private Function IImportCropHandler_Crop(ByVal Options As IStructImportCropOptions) As Boolean
    Options.Left = 0: Options.Top = 0
    Options.Width = Options.ImageWidth \ 2   ' left half
    Options.Height = Options.ImageHeight
    IImportCropHandler_Crop = True
End Function

cards.name: IStructImportResampleOptions
cards.summary: Options object CorelDRAW hands to an import resample handler (IImportResampleHandler.Resample) when a bitmap is imported in resample mode: read-only FileName, FilterID and CustomData, and the writable target Width, Height, DpiX and DpiY the handler sets. The typelib gives no member descriptions, so the roles follow the names and read-only flags.
use_for: downsampling oversized photos to a print resolution while importing a batch
per-file resample rules (e.g. cap every image at 300 dpi at its placed size)
avoid: the same resample for every file: set StructImportOptions.Mode = cdrImportResample and its ResampleWidth / ResampleHeight / ResampleDpiX / ResampleDpiY instead of writing a handler
upsampling to 'improve' quality: resampling up adds no detail
cards.how: Not created by scripts: an object implementing IImportResampleHandler is set as StructImportOptions.ResampleHandler, Mode is cdrImportResample, and CorelDRAW passes this object to its Resample method during Layer.ImportEx (flow unverified).

key_members.name: CustomData
key_members.use: read-only: caller data passed through to the handler

gotchas: there is no ImageWidth / ImageHeight here; Width / Height presumably arrive filled with the source size (unverified)
Width / Height are long integers, most likely pixels (unverified)
Resample returns a Boolean; the effect of returning False is not in the harvest (unverified)
cards.example:
' VBA class module, set as StructImportOptions.ResampleHandler (unverified)
Implements IImportResampleHandler
Private Function IImportResampleHandler_Resample(ByVal Options As IStructImportResampleOptions) As Boolean
    Options.Width = Options.Width \ 2
    Options.Height = Options.Height \ 2
    Options.DpiX = 300: Options.DpiY = 300
    IImportResampleHandler_Resample = True
End Function

cards.name: IVGActiveView
cards.summary: The live view of a CorelDRAW document window: which part of the page is on screen and how it is drawn. It sets zoom and origin, fits the view to the page, page width or height, a shape, a shape range, the selection, all objects, all pages or an area, zooms in and out, sets 1:1, switches the view type (wireframe, draft, normal, enhanced, pixel, enhanced with overprints), overprint simulation and on-screen colour proofing, and handles Multipage view (page at a point, page origins, page bounds).
use_for: framing the page before a screenshot for a contact sheet or QC frame
Pixel view checks of web and social graphics at actual size
on-screen soft proof with a press profile before printing
checking spot and black overprints with SimulateOverprints
avoid: controlling export output: the view does not change exports; use Document.Export / ExportBitmap
screenshots of a minimized CorelDRAW window: nothing is drawn; restore AppWindow first
cards.how: Application.ActiveWindow.ActiveView (the ActiveView of any Window). One per document window; changes are visual only and are not stored as artwork. Named saved views are a different object (Document.CreateView / Views).

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrViewType: cdrSimpleWireframeView, cdrWireframeView, cdrDraftView, cdrNormalView, cdrEnhancedView, cdrEnhancedViewWithOverprints, cdrPixelView

key_members.name: OriginX
key_members.use: x of the view origin (document units)

key_members.name: OriginY
key_members.use: y of the view origin (document units)

key_members.name: SetViewPoint
key_members.use: centre the view on x, y with an optional zoom

key_members.name: ToFitArea
key_members.use: fit a Left / Top / Right / Bottom rectangle

key_members.name: ShowProofColors
key_members.use: display colour proofing in this window

key_members.name: ProofColorSettings
key_members.use: the proofing profile settings used for this window

key_members.name: UseMultipageView
key_members.use: switch the window to Multipage view

key_members.name: FindPageAtPoint
key_members.use: the page under a point in Multipage view

gotchas: the Zoom scale is not in the harvest; call SetActualSize and read Zoom to learn the 1:1 value before setting Zoom directly
GetViewArea returns its four values through ByRef arguments; from Python win32com they may come back as a tuple or not at all, depending on the typelib's out flags (unverified)
OriginX / OriginY and area coordinates follow the document's Unit setting
FindPageAtPoint, GetPageOrigin and SetPageOrigin are Multipage view features; with UseMultipageView off they may fail or only see the active page (unverified)
ToFitShape / ToFitSelection with nothing selected raises an error; check the selection first (unverified)
cards.example:
With ActiveWindow.ActiveView
    .Type = cdrEnhancedView
    .ToFitPage
    Debug.Print .Zoom, .OriginX, .OriginY
    .SimulateOverprints = True
End With

review.changes: gotcha: replaced the invented "Zoom 100 = actual size" with reading Zoom after SetActualSize (scale not in the harvest)

cards.name: IVGApplication
cards.summary: The CorelDRAW application object, root of the whole object model: documents (open, create, from template, open as copy), the active document, page, layer, window, selection and tool, colour factories (RGB, CMYK, Lab, HSB, spot, palette), option-struct factories for open / save / export / import / paste, unit conversion, fonts, palettes, printers and the multi-document print job, workspaces, command bars and the UI FrameWork, version and folder paths, event hookup and the speed switches Optimization and EventsEnabled.
use_for: entry point of every CorelDRAW automation: open a template, fill it, export
batch processing a folder of .cdr files
making brand colours (CMYK values, spot colours by name) for scripted artwork
version and install-path checks in a pipeline preflight
speeding up long macros with Optimization
avoid: Quit while a person may be using CorelDRAW: closes it for everyone, and save prompts can block the COM call
ActiveDocument / ActiveSelection in unattended pipelines: they follow whatever the user focused; keep the Document returned by OpenDocument / CreateDocument
cards.how: Inside CorelDRAW VBA: the global Application object (its members also work as globals: ActiveDocument, ActiveLayer ...). From outside: COM, e.g. Python win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25") for CorelDRAW 2024 (the harvest finds this ProgID registered to the 25 install), or C# through the VGCore interop. Never the bare "CorelDRAW.Application": its CurVer on this machine is CorelDRAW.Application.23 (CorelDRAW 2021).

key_members.name: ActiveDocument
key_members.use: the document in the active window (Nothing when none is open)

key_members.name: OpenDocument
key_members.use: open a file; returns the Document

key_members.name: CreateDocument
key_members.use: new document from the default template

key_members.name: CreateDocumentEx
key_members.use: new document with StructCreateOptions (Name, PageWidth, PageHeight, Units, Resolution, Bleed, ColorContext)

key_members.name: CreateDocumentFromTemplate
key_members.use: new document from a .cdt template, optionally with its graphics

key_members.name: ActiveLayer
key_members.use: the active layer (where new shapes go)

key_members.name: ActiveWindow
key_members.use: active document window (its ActiveView controls zoom)

key_members.name: CreateSpotColorByName
key_members.use: a spot colour from a palette by name, with optional tint

key_members.name: CreateShapeRange
key_members.use: an empty ShapeRange to collect shapes

key_members.name: ConvertUnits
key_members.use: convert a value between cdrUnit units

key_members.name: Optimization
key_members.use: suspend screen updates for speed during long macros

key_members.name: EventsEnabled
key_members.use: switch event handlers on or off

key_members.name: Visible
key_members.use: show or hide the application window

gotchas: Optimization = True stops screen updates for speed; always set it back to False (also in the error handler) and refresh the window (ActiveWindow.Refresh), or the UI looks stale
EventsEnabled = False keeps event macros from firing during batch work; restore it afterwards
ActiveSelection returns one Shape wrapping the selection; ActiveSelectionRange returns a ShapeRange snapshot that does not follow later selection changes (unverified)
Unit only applies when there is no document context; shape coordinates follow Document.Unit
started through COM the app may come up hidden; set Visible = True before relying on windows or views (unverified)
modal dialogs (missing fonts on OpenDocument, save prompts on Quit) block the COM call; give every call a timeout

the unversioned ProgID "CorelDRAW.Application" resolves (CurVer) to CorelDRAW.Application.23, the CorelDRAW 2021 install also registered on this machine; always dispatch "CorelDRAW.Application.25" and check VersionMajor = 25
cards.example:
import win32com.client
app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")  # not the bare ProgID (= v23)
app.Visible = True
doc = app.OpenDocument(r"E:\in\poster.cdr")
app.Optimization = True; app.EventsEnabled = False
# ... edit doc ...
app.Optimization = False; app.EventsEnabled = True
app.ActiveWindow.Refresh()

review.changes: how/example: ProgID CorelDRAW.Application.25 is in the harvest (HKCR), no longer "unverified"; added gotcha that the bare CorelDRAW.Application CurVer is .23 (CorelDRAW 2021); CreateDocumentEx use now lists the real StructCreateOptions fields instead of "colour mode"

cards.name: IVGApplicationEvents
cards.summary: Hidden dual twin of the CorelDRAW application event interface (the Application and GlobalMacroStorage coclasses declare DIVGApplicationEvents, with the same 22 events and dispids, as their source): callbacks a handler receives for document open, new and close, before / after save, print and export, the Query* events that let the handler cancel a close, save, print, export or quit, window activate / deactivate, selection change, application start and quit, plug-in command execution and enable / check state updates, and a generic OnApplicationEvent.
use_for: running a preflight automatically before every export or save
blocking a close or quit while a job is unsaved on a shared workstation
logging which files were exported and where
handling plug-in commands registered with Application.AddPluginCommand
avoid: heavy work in SelectionChange: it fires on every selection change and slows the UI; keep handlers short
relying on events while Application.EventsEnabled is False: nothing fires
cards.how: Implemented, not called. The connection point CorelDRAW fires is DIVGApplicationEvents; this dual IVGApplicationEvents carries the same members for sinks that implement the dual interface (unverified). VBA: a class module with Public WithEvents app As CorelDRAW.Application, then Set app = Application, or handlers in a GMS ThisMacroStorage module named GlobalMacroStorage_<Event>. External COM clients: Application.AdviseEvents(sink) returns a cookie and Application.UnadviseEvents(cookie) stops delivery. Flagged hidden in the typelib.

key_members.name: QueryDocumentClose
key_members.use: before a close; set Cancel = True to keep the document open

key_members.name: QueryDocumentSave
key_members.use: before a save; Cancel stops it

key_members.name: QueryDocumentExport
key_members.use: before an export; Cancel stops it

key_members.name: QueryQuit
key_members.use: before the app quits; Cancel stops it

key_members.name: DocumentOpen
key_members.use: a document was opened (with its file name)

key_members.name: DocumentNew
key_members.use: a document was created (template info included)

key_members.name: DocumentBeforeSave
key_members.use: about to save (SaveAs flag, file name)

key_members.name: DocumentBeforeExport
key_members.use: about to export (file name, filter, bitmap flag)

key_members.name: OnPluginCommand
key_members.use: a registered plug-in command was run (CommandID)

key_members.name: OnUpdatePluginCommand
key_members.use: CorelDRAW asks for a plug-in command's Enabled / Checked state

key_members.name: OnApplicationEvent
key_members.use: generic event: name plus a SAFEARRAY of parameters

gotchas: Cancel in the Query* events is a ByRef Boolean: set it True to stop the action (unverified)
the Query* events are described as fired when the user responds to a request, so a script-driven save or close may not raise them (unverified)
event procedure signatures must match the typelib exactly; let the VBA editor's event dropdown generate them
a sink registered with AdviseEvents must be removed with UnadviseEvents before the client exits (unverified)
which names OnApplicationEvent delivers is not in the harvest (unverified)
WithEvents and DispatchWithEvents bind to the coclass source DIVGApplicationEvents, not to this interface; the event names and parameters are identical
cards.example:
' VBA class module; elsewhere: Set obj.app = Application
Public WithEvents app As CorelDRAW.Application
Private Sub app_QueryDocumentClose(ByVal Doc As Document, Cancel As Boolean)
    If Doc.Dirty Then Cancel = True   ' keep unsaved work open
End Sub
Private Sub app_DocumentAfterExport(ByVal Doc As Document, ByVal FileName As String, ByVal Filter As cdrFilter, ByVal SaveBitmap As Boolean)
    Debug.Print "exported " & FileName
End Sub

review.changes: summary/how: it is not the Application source interface; the Application and GlobalMacroStorage coclasses source DIVGApplicationEvents (identical 22 events/dispids), this is its dual twin; added the GMS ThisMacroStorage route and a gotcha

cards.name: IVGAppPlugin
cards.summary: Hidden interface a compiled CorelDRAW plug-in implements so the application can load it: OnLoad receives the Application object, StartSession and StopSession bracket the working session, and OnUnload is the last call before the plug-in is released. The typelib gives no descriptions; the roles follow the names.
use_for: building a compiled (C++) CorelDRAW plug-in that adds commands to the UI
a studio tool that keeps a live connection to CorelDRAW instead of relaunching scripts
avoid: one-off automation: a VBA / GMS macro or an external COM script is far simpler
calling these members from a script: they are callbacks CorelDRAW makes, not methods to run
cards.how: Implemented, not called. Native .cpg plug-ins in CorelDRAW's Plugins folder export an AttachPlugin function that hands CorelDRAW an IVGAppPlugin pointer (unverified); commands are then registered with Application.AddPluginCommand and arrive through the OnPluginCommand event.

key_members.name: OnLoad
key_members.use: first call; receives the IVGApplication to keep

key_members.name: StartSession
key_members.use: the session starts: register commands, hook events

key_members.name: StopSession
key_members.use: the session ends: remove commands, unhook events

key_members.name: OnUnload
key_members.use: last call before release: drop the Application reference

gotchas: keep the Application reference from OnLoad and release it in OnUnload, or CorelDRAW may not shut down cleanly (unverified)
register commands in StartSession and remove them in StopSession (Application.AddPluginCommand / RemovePluginCommand) (unverified)
a plug-in built against another major version's type library may need a rebuild for version 25 (unverified)

cards.name: IVGAppStatus
cards.summary: The status-bar progress meter of CorelDRAW (Application.Status): a script shows it with an optional message and an Esc-to-abort option, moves it (Progress or UpdateProgress), changes its message, reads Aborted to see whether the user pressed Esc, and hides it with EndProgress.
use_for: feedback during a long macro (recolouring hundreds of shapes, exporting many pages)
letting the designer cancel a long batch with Esc
avoid: unattended COM pipelines with nobody watching: log to a file instead
updating on every item of a very tight loop: update every N items to keep redraw cost down (unverified)
cards.how: Application.Status (read-only reference to the AppStatus object).

key_members.name: BeginProgress
key_members.use: show the meter, optional message and CanAbort (Esc) flag

key_members.name: SetProgressMessage
key_members.use: change the message shown with the meter

key_members.name: Aborted
key_members.use: True once the user pressed Esc

gotchas: always call EndProgress, including in the error handler, or the meter stays on the status bar (unverified)
Aborted presumably only turns True when BeginProgress was called with CanAbort = True (unverified)
the Progress scale (0-100?) and what UpdateProgress's Step does are not in the harvest (unverified)
cards.example:
Set st = Application.Status
n = ActivePage.Shapes.Count
st.BeginProgress "Recolouring shapes...", True
For i = 1 To n
    st.Progress = Int(i * 100 / n)   ' 0-100 scale assumed (unverified)
    If st.Aborted Then Exit For
Next i
st.EndProgress

cards.name: IVGAppWindow
cards.summary: The CorelDRAW main application window (Application.AppWindow): its caption, position and size, client area size, window state (normal, minimized, maximized, restore), whether it is active, its native window handle, and Activate to bring it to the front.
use_for: maximizing and activating CorelDRAW before screenshots
getting the window handle for PostMessage / UI Automation aimed at CorelDRAW instead of global keystrokes
a fixed window size so view-based screenshots are repeatable
putting a job name in the window caption on a shared machine
avoid: document windows: those are Window objects (Application.ActiveWindow / Windows)
Activate while a person is working on the machine: it steals focus
cards.how: Application.AppWindow (read-only reference to the AppWindow object).

key_members.name: Handle
key_members.use: native window handle (HWND) of the main window

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: bring the main window to the front

key_members.name: Active
key_members.use: read-only: is the main window active

gotchas: Handle is a 32-bit long; on 64-bit Windows it can be used as the HWND as is (window handles fit in 32 bits) (unverified)
a minimized window draws nothing, so screen captures come back blank: set WindowState to cdrWindowNormal or cdrWindowMaximized first
Left / Top / Width / Height are screen pixels and may be ignored while the window is maximized (unverified)
CorelDRAW may rewrite Caption when the active document changes (unverified)
cards.example:
w = app.AppWindow
w.WindowState = 3          # cdrWindowMaximized
w.Activate()
print(w.Caption, w.ClientWidth, w.ClientHeight)
hwnd = w.Handle            # for PostMessage / UI Automation targeting

cards.name: IVGArrowHead
cards.summary: One arrowhead definition (the shape drawn at a line end), from the application's arrowhead list or made from a curve: its index in the list, the curve that draws it, outline-width scale, centre point and line offset (how far the line is shortened to meet the arrow), name and display name, a copy bound to a document, and a sameness test.
use_for: arrows on callout and leader lines
technical drawings and dimension lines
flowcharts and infographics built by script
checking that all connectors in a diagram use the same arrow style
avoid: sizing, offsetting or flipping an arrow: not here; use Outline.StartArrowOptions / EndArrowOptions
choosing arrows by index across machines or versions: the list can differ; match by Name / DisplayName or CompareWith
cards.how: Application.ArrowHeads(i) (the installed arrowhead list), Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow of a shape, or Document.CreateArrowHead / CreateArrowHeadEx for a custom one from a curve. Apply it with Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow or Outline.SetProperties.

key_members.name: Index
key_members.use: read-only position in the arrowhead list

key_members.name: DisplayName
key_members.use: read-only name; generated when no custom name is set

key_members.name: Curve
key_members.use: read-only Curve that draws the arrowhead

key_members.name: CenterX
key_members.use: relative horizontal centre of the arrowhead

key_members.name: CenterY
key_members.use: relative vertical centre of the arrowhead

key_members.name: BaseOutlineScale
key_members.use: outline width relative to the arrowhead curve

key_members.name: LineOffset
key_members.use: relative amount the line is shortened to fit the arrow

key_members.name: BindToDocument
key_members.use: copy that reports coordinates in a given document's system

key_members.name: CompareWith
key_members.use: True when two arrowheads are the same

gotchas: almost everything is read-only; to change the shape create a new arrowhead from a curve (Document.CreateArrowHead)
CenterX / CenterY / BaseOutlineScale / LineOffset are relative values; call BindToDocument to read them in a document's coordinates
Name may be empty for built-in arrowheads; DisplayName then returns a generated name
compare arrowheads with CompareWith, not by object identity (unverified)
cards.example:
Set ah = Application.ArrowHeads(5)
Debug.Print ah.Index, ah.DisplayName
ActiveShape.Outline.SetProperties EndArrow:=ah
If ActiveShape.Outline.EndArrow.CompareWith(ah) Then Debug.Print "arrow set"
